key_insight: Visual autoregressive (VAR) models suffer from asynchronous policy conflicts because each generation step sees heterogeneous inputs; aligning policies across these steps via group-relative updates stabilizes RL training and improves alignment.
problem_solved: The paper addresses unstable and suboptimal reinforcement learning for Visual Autoregressive generation caused by asynchronous policy conflicts that arise from varying input structures across generation steps.
method: Partition generation steps into consistent 'groups' based on input/conditioning heterogeneity and treat each group as a related sub-policy.

Perform group-relative policy optimization: update policies with constraints/regularizers that enforce consistency across groups (relative updates, KL/consistency penalties) rather than independent asynchronous updates.
Integrate these updates into the RL training loop for VARs to reduce conflicting gradients and stabilize optimization (e.g., prioritized replay or group-aware advantage estimation).
impact: Provides a practical recipe to stabilize RL for VAR models, enabling more reliable alignment and higher-quality visual generation—useful for practitioners training multimodal/autoregressive generators under RL objectives.
visual_elements: Diagram showing heterogeneous inputs across time steps with arrows indicating asynchronous conflicts, contrasted with grouped steps and synchronized arrows after GRPO.

paper_title: VAR RL Done Right: Tackling Asynchronous Policy Conflicts in Visual Autoregressive Generation
paper_authors: Shikun Sun, Liao Qu, Huichao Zhang, Yiheng Liu, Yangyang Song
